title: Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval
layout_note: Two stages side by side: item-to-ID tokenisation (a small loop over a table) at left, a sequence encoder-decoder over ID tokens at right.
grouping: Two stages side by side without frames. Left: a ruled item table (ItemID, Title, Description, Categories, Brand, then a separate Semantic ID column); a highlighted row is circled by a red outline and a dark-red curved arrow leads down to a row of process boxes whose result loops back up by an orange curved arrow into the Semantic ID cell. Right: a wide encoder box and a decoder box joined by a hollow grey block arrow labelled 'Encoded Context'; a curly brace beneath the encoder's inputs reads 'Item Interaction History of User 5', a brace above the decoder's output reads 'Next Item'.
shapes_depth: Rounded rectangles with thin outlines, flat: 'Item Content Information' pale red, 'Content Encoder' a light-blue trapezoid, 'Embedding' a narrow vertical blue bar with rotated text, 'Quantization' orange. The encoder and decoder are wide pale-yellow rounded boxes. Tokens are small light-grey boxes (t_u5, t_5, t_23, t_55, <BOS>, <EOS>) with thin grey arrows into the model; the user token's label sits on a small green box, and each history item is an orange box reading 'Item 233 / Sem. ID = (5, 23, 55)' beneath its three code tokens. Sans-serif text throughout.
proposed_highlight: Orange is reserved for the paper's item representation: the Quantization box, every item box carrying a semantic ID tuple and the predicted next item; the generic encoder and decoder stay pale yellow and the tokens grey.
lesson: Render each item in the user's history as an orange box carrying its ID tuple, with the tuple's code tokens as a row of small grey boxes directly above it, so the reader sees both the item and the tokens the sequence model actually reads.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF's first page (NeurIPS 2023). layout 'other': item tokenisation at left feeding a sequence encoder-decoder at right. elements 'matrix' = the ruled item table; 'other' = the loop-back arrow writing into the table. The `refs crop` record lists one embedded raster region covering the left stage (item table and tokenisation boxes, a drawn diagram, not a photo), so photo_share counts that drawn part and the palette leaves it out.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: every item is drawn as an orange box carrying its Semantic ID tuple ('Item 233, Sem. ID = (5, 23, 55)') with that tuple's codeword tokens t_5, t_23, t_55 as grey boxes above it, so a user's history visibly becomes a token sequence that an encoder reads and a decoder continues

relations.form: two unframed panels side by side: on the left the semantic-ID construction, on the right generative retrieval over those IDs; orange links the Quantization box on the left to the item boxes on the right

left panel: a red curved arrow leaves a highlighted row of an item table (ItemID, Title, Description, Categories, Brand) down to Item Content Information -> Content Encoder trapezoid -> vertical Embedding bar -> Quantization, and an orange curved arrow returns up into the table's separate Semantic ID column
right panel: a green User_5 box with token t_u5, then two orange item boxes each with three grey token boxes above it, bracketed below as 'Item Interaction History of User 5'
a hollow block arrow labelled 'Encoded Context' runs straight from the yellow Bidirectional Transformer Encoder to the yellow Transformer Decoder
the decoder's inputs '<BOS> t_5 t_25 t_55' sit below it and its outputs 't_5 t_25 t_55 <EOS>' above it, shifted by one, topped by the orange 'Item 64, Sem. ID = (5, 25, 55)' bracketed as 'Next Item'

channels.colour: fill = kind of element: orange = semantic IDs (the Quantization step and every item box), red = raw item content, blue = content encoder and embedding, pale yellow = the two transformers, green = the user token, grey = individual tokens - one meaning each
channels.shape: a table = the item catalogue; trapezoid = encoder; thin vertical bar = embedding vector; rounded boxes = modules; small square boxes = tokens
channels.line: thin grey arrows = token inputs and outputs; red and orange curves = taking content from and writing IDs back into the table; a '//' mark on the embedding-to-quantization arrow is unexplained; hollow block arrow = encoder context

quality.strengths: the data are drawn as data - a catalogue table with real column names, items with literal Semantic ID tuples, and tokens whose numbers match the tuples (t_5, t_23, t_55 under (5, 23, 55)), so the reader can trace how an item becomes tokens; orange consistently marks semantic IDs across both panels
quality.weaknesses: the semantic-ID construction, the paper's new step, is the smaller left panel and its Quantization is one box that does not show how three codewords arise; the two panels have no frames or labels; the left panel's loop leaves and re-enters the table by long curves, and the '//' on the embedding arrow is not keyed

insights.structure: Two unframed halves: left an item table (ItemID, Title, Description, Categories, Brand | Semantic ID) above a loop Item Content -> Content Encoder -> Embedding -> Quantization; right a bidirectional Transformer encoder feeding a Transformer decoder.
insights.data: Semantic IDs are shown as concrete tuples (Item 233 = (5,23,55)) in orange boxes and expanded into grey token chips t_5, t_23, t_55 under the encoder; the user is a green User_5 chip.
insights.emphasis: Orange is used consistently for anything semantic-ID: the Quantization box, the table's Semantic ID column, item boxes and the predicted Next Item (Item 64).
insights.flow: Left half loops: red arrow from a table row down to content, right through encoder to quantization, orange arrow back up into the Semantic ID column; right half reads bottom (tokens) to encoder, right through a hollow 'Encoded Context' arrow to the decoder, up to the next item.
insights.avoid: The two halves are not labelled as stages (a)/(b) nor linked by any arrow, so the reader must infer that the left produces the IDs the right consumes.

arrangement.units: two unframed side-by-side regions (ID generation, then sequence model) with no titles
arrangement.inputs_as: item table rows on the left; token chips with concrete semantic-ID values under the encoder on the right
arrangement.shared: semantic-ID colour (orange) ties the two halves
